title: Josip and Anna, with Ante
caption: A studio portrait: Josip seated in a light suit and loose cravat, Anna in a dark bodice with the high collar and gathered shoulders of the 1890s, the baby Ante across her lap in a striped romper. The painted backdrop and the vignetted edge are the marks of a small provincial photographer.

title: Zane Defranceschi
caption: A man in a white peaked cap, shirtsleeves and wide trousers, seated on a rush-bottomed chair against a whitewashed wall, a barefoot boy leaning on his shoulder. Zane is the Venetian form of Giovanni — the same name the parish clerks wrote as Zuane.

title: Zane, middle front
caption: A group photograph kept with the Omiš papers; the family's note places Zane in the middle of the front row.

title: Anton “Toni” Franceschi, 1932
caption: Dated by the family to 1932. Note the surname as written on the print: Franceschi, without the particle — the Omiš branch dropped and resumed it by turns.

title: Frane Defranceski
caption: Frane is the Croatian form of Francesco; the surname on this print is spelled the Croatian way, Defranceski.

title: Carlo De Franceschi in old age
caption: The historian of Istria, born at Gologorica in 1809, photographed late in life: round spectacles, white beard, dark stock. He died in 1893.

title: Petar Defranceski — Fiche Individuelle
caption: The French-zone camp card. Petar, born 15 June 1913 at Crikvenica, Yugoslav, profession auto-mécanicien, employer's address Kelterstr. 30 Neuhausen, married. Five fingerprints in red, a passport photograph clipped at the top right, file 148.902 / 30609.

title: Zdrafko Defranceski — Fiche Individuelle
caption: Born 1 April 1921, Yugoslav, auto-mécanicien, married. File 148.901 / 30560. The same trade as Petar, and the same camp office.

title: Ruža Defranceski — Fiche Individuelle
caption: Born 1922, no profession recorded, married. In the photograph she wears a cross at her throat and holds her infant son, who is not named here: he was born in 1944 and may be living.

title: Foreigners registered at Pfullingen, 1939–45
caption: “Aufstellung über die in der Zeit vom 1. Sept. 1939 – 25. April 1945 in der Vorstadt Pfullingen gemeldet gewesenen Ausländer. Hier: Kroatien.” Drawn up at Reutlingen-Pfullingen on 10 March 1947. Six Defranceskis are listed, five of them born at Crikvenica.

title: ITS file cover D-1.505
caption: The tracing-service wrapper for the family: Petar, his wife Luise née Salzer of Neuhausen, and two daughters born at Urach and Metzingen during the war.

title: CM/1 application, identity page
caption: The IRO care-and-maintenance application, 7 November 1947. Petar gives his nationality at birth as Austria-Hungary, his address as Kelternstr. 30 Neuhausen, and the country he wants to be resettled in as the United States — California.

title: CM/1 application, history page
caption: Residences, trades and schooling: Split 1937–39 with Jugoslav Lloyd as a ship's engineer, then Germany from April 1939; car-mechanic examination at Reutlingen in 1947; a truck valued at 15,000 among his assets; and an aunt, Jacomina Alafetić, at San Pedro, California.

title: Felix Defranceski — sickness-fund card
caption: Felix, born 1908 at Crikvenica, single, living at Pfullingerlandstraße in Reutlingen. Employers from July 1941: Hermann Sauer of Pfullingen as a motor mechanic, then Wilhelm Heim as a driver, then Sauer again.

title: Ivan Defranceski — sickness-fund card
caption: Ivan, born June 1925 at Crikvenica, single, Brunnenstraße 7, Pfullingen. He entered work on 21 October 1941, aged sixteen, as a Hilfsarbeiter — an unskilled hand.

title: Petar Defranceski — sickness-fund card
caption: Marked “Kroate” in the top margin. Employed by Hermann Sauer of Reutlingen on motor-vehicle repairs from 1 April 1942 to 2 March 1945 — the card runs out three weeks before the French army reached the town.

title: Zdravko Defranceski — sickness-fund card
caption: Below the employment lines, a clerk has pencilled a short life: in Croatia 1936–43; taken by the Partisans in 1943; three or four months in captivity; then straight to Germany.

title: Anton Defranceski, born 1890 — municipal certificate
caption: Certified by the mayor of Pfullingen, Kreis Reutlingen, on 28 February 1950: Anton Defranceski, born 20 January 1890 at Crikvenica, Croatia-Yugoslavia, lodged at Pfullingen, workplace Hermann Sauer, Reutlingen-Süd.

title: Resettlement roll, February 1949
caption: Lines 58–60 of a nominal roll dated 22 February 1949: Zdrafko, Ruža and their son, Yugoslavs from Crikvenica and Fužine, at Reutlingen, with IRO numbers against each name.

title: Državni arhiv u Pazinu to David Defranceski, 26 April 2021
caption: The Pazin State Archive answers a request made eight days earlier: the copy from the Gračišće birth register for Josip Defranceschi is enclosed. Itemised at 117 kuna — research 50, certified A3 copy 7, overseas postage 60.

title: Liber Baptizatorum, Gračišće 1841–1899
caption: Certified and stamped by the Pazin State Archive. The register is ruled for house number, the child's name and date of birth, religion, sex, legitimacy, both parents with the father's condition, the godparents and the midwife. The entry taken out for this family is Josephus, born 22 March 1863, son of Antonius Defranceschi, lapicida — a stonecutter.
holder: Državni arhiv u Pazinu (DAPA), MKR Gračišće 1841–1899

title: Državni arhiv u Pazinu, 24 June 2021
caption: A second answer, this time for Antonius Defranceschi and his family, and for Giovanni Battista Defranceschi and his family — the two Status Animarum entries opposite. 124 kuna.

title: Status Animarum — house 5, Gallignana
caption: The book of souls for the parish of Gallignana. House 5: Joan. Bapt. Defranceschi, agricola, born 13 August 1787, married 1819, died 1 September 1846; his wife Francisca Salomon, born 17 March 1797; and their sons Raymundus, Antonius, Joannes and Franciscus.
holder: Državni arhiv u Pazinu (DAPA), ZM34K 217, M01072071

title: Status Animarum — house 19, Gallignana
caption: House 19: † Antonius Defranceschi q. Joannis — son of the late Giovanni — born 20 September 1825, married 25 November 1856, died 4 August 1894; his wife Maria née Fernasar, born 17 October 1832; and their children Antonius, Josephus, Leopolda, Catharina and Modestus.
holder: Državni arhiv u Pazinu (DAPA), ZM34K 217, M01071656

title: Anna Kalanj, born 3 January 1864
caption: Entry 2 for 1864 in the baptismal register of Ledenice, the Vinodol parish above Crikvenica. Anna, legitimate, daughter of Josephus Kalanj and Rosalia née Perković, at Rijenovica house 22; godparents Josephus Ban and his wife Anna; baptised by Vincentius Segulja, parish priest. The other entries on the page are Perković, Butković, Mataija, Semper — the surnames of one valley.

title: Carlo De Franceschi signs as a witness, Pazin 1842
caption: The Pisino marriage register, 13 September 1842. Antonius Covach, 22, of house 33, marries Hedwiges Mrak, 17, of house 30. In the column for witnesses: «Carolus Defranceschi» and «Aegidius Mrach», and against their names their conditions — «I. R. Auscultans» and «studiosus». Imperial-Royal Auscultator was the entry rank of the Austrian judicial service. Carlo was thirty-two.

title: Anton Rudolf, born 20 January 1890
caption: Entry 9 in the Croatian-language baptismal register: Anton Rudolf, born 20 January 1890, baptised 9 February, legitimate, son of «Josip Defranceschi i žena Ana Kalanj rodjena». Residence: Klenovica house 22 — and beside it, in the column for the parents' place of origin, «Gallignana u Istriji». Godfather Jakov Kalanj of the same house 22; baptised by Matej Butković, parish priest.

title: Nodburga Defranceschi marries at Bakar, 1794
caption: 27 February 1794, dispensed from the third banns by the Bishop: in the church of the Blessed Virgin Mary, the marriage of Dominus Joannes Vorkret and Domicella Nodburga Defranceschi, blessed by Canon Antonius de Agnesis, in the presence of the Vice-Governor Aloysius de Orlando and the noble Antonio Maria ab Orebich, assessor of the community of Buccari. Notburga is a Tyrolean saint's name, and an odd one to find on the Kvarner coast.

title: Antonio Defranceschi of Zara — refused
caption: A second IRO application, completed at Bolzano on 10 May 1950. Antonio Defranceschi, born 18 January 1905 at Zara, ethnic group Italian, son of Riccardo and Giuseppina Zersuscek; his wife Antonietta née Stipanovich, born 1910, daughter of Sabino Stipanovich and Maria Lovrich. Clerk at Zara to 1941, then a soldier in the Italian army until the capitulation, then Zara again until January 1944, then Italy. Twice across the form, in blue crayon: NOT WITHIN THE MANDATE OF IRO.

title: Edoardo De Franceschi dies at San Daniele del Friuli, 1899
caption: Atti di morte no. 28, San Daniele del Friuli, 12 August 1899: at five in the morning there died in the Civic Hospital «De Franceschi Edoardo, di anni quarantotto, già Ufficiale, nato in Zara e domiciliato in Zara, figlio del fu Giovanni e della fu Zenardi Maria, coniugato a Pappafava Regina» — a former officer of Zadar, forty-eight, seven hundred kilometres from home.
holder: Comune di San Daniele del Friuli, Atti di morte

title: Pietro De Franceschi dies at San Daniele del Friuli, 1895
caption: Atti di morte no. 19, 30 March 1895, in the same hospital four years earlier: «De Franceschi Pietro, di anni quarantaquattro, mura…» — a mason, forty-four. The trade of the Gračišće line, in the country the family says it came from.
holder: Comune di San Daniele del Friuli, Atti di morte

title: Josip “Bepo” de Franceschi
caption: A hand-tinted studio portrait, one of a matched pair with the woman opposite — almost certainly a marriage pair. Dark hair swept back, a full beard, a bow tie. The family file dates him 1870; the Gračišće register makes the man of this name and place born 22 March 1863.

title: Ana, the companion portrait
caption: The other half of the pair: a young woman in a high-necked dress with lace at the cuffs, hair dressed up, hand resting on a chair back. Tinted the same warm brown by the same hand.

title: The grave of Ana de Franceschi
caption: A standing stone with a cross and two oval porcelain medallions — a woman, and a man in a fedora. «Ovdje počiva u miru Božjem — ANA DE. FRANCESCHI — ✱ 19.IX.1863 ✝ 28.V.1936». Here rests in God's peace. Below the dates the word «suprug», husband, begins a second inscription that the photograph cuts off.

title: Ursula, born Kovačina
caption: Anton Rudolf's wife, and the mother of the four brothers who ended up in Württemberg. Seated, in the loose drop-waisted dress of the early 1920s, something folded in her lap. The print is worn to the emulsion at every corner.

title: Ursula in old age, with a grandchild
caption: Colour, 1960s or 70s. She sits among stacked café chairs on a seafront, a small child standing against her knee, a traffic policeman in white passing behind. The child is not named here.

title: Petar Defranceski
caption: A studio portrait in a double-breasted pinstripe. Set this beside the photograph clipped to his French camp card in 1947 and it is plainly the same man: the same long jaw, the same swept hair.

title: “Peter (Senior), pilot in war”
caption: A young man in a leather flying helmet with the goggles pushed up on his forehead, and a sheepskin-collared flying jacket. The family's own caption calls him Peter Senior, a pilot in the war. Nothing in the displaced-persons file mentions flying: there he is a ship's engineer with Jugoslav Lloyd, and then a motor mechanic.

title: Zdravko Defranceski
caption: A studio portrait in a wide-lapelled pinstripe suit, hair oiled back — the same face as the French camp card of 1947, a few years and a good deal of trouble apart.

title: Zdravko's plaque at Horsham
caption: «In loving remembrance of ZDRAVKO FRANK DEFRANCESKI, died 22nd December 1979 aged 58, beloved husband of Rosa, loved father of Anton and Vivian, loved grandfather of Dean, Lisa, Antonia and Carla. Resting in God's loving care.» A bronze plaque in a lawn cemetery in the Victorian Wimmera, for a man born at Crikvenica.

title: Ruža, born Hreljac
caption: A young woman with a flower pinned in her hair, photographed in the 1940s. Born at Fužine on 13 February 1922; died 30 January 1996 and buried at Horsham beside Zdravko.

title: The grave of Ivan Defrančeski, 1925–1995
caption: Polished dark granite, a plain incised cross, and the name cut in Croatian orthography: IVAN DEFRANČESKI, 1925–1995. Flowers and photographs on the neighbouring slabs. The boy who entered a Reutlingen factory at sixteen in October 1941 went home, and is buried on his own coast.

title: Anton, as a boy
caption: The child written on the French camp card in 1947 with the single word «enfant» across the fingerprint boxes, and photographed that year in his mother's arms. Here he is a few years older, in a dark pinafore over a knitted jumper. The print is torn across one corner. He died at Ipswich, Queensland, in 1999.

title: Pepe, centre, with four sailors
caption: Five young men in naval ratings' uniform and round caps, shoulder to shoulder against a hedge. The family caption puts Pepe in the middle. Interwar, and the Adriatic: these are Yugoslav navy caps.

title: Pepe on the sea wall
caption: A man in shirtsleeves sitting on a harbour parapet, a bay and a low waterfront behind him, boats out on the water. The photographer's blindstamp in the corner reads ZORA.

title: Stancija Seghetto — the manor house
caption: The front Giorgio de Franceschi (1788–1865) commissioned in 1843–45: two giant pilasters flanking the centre, two orders of six windows, a great round-arched portal, and a tympanum over all. Neoclassical, in the manner of the second quarter of the nineteenth century, grafted onto a Venetian country house of the seventeenth.

title: The arms in the tympanum
caption: A circular medallion set in the pediment, with a shield carved in relief inside it, and below, lozenge panels with rosettes. La Voce del popolo records the arms here as «troncato di azzurro e d'oro al leone rampante al naturale». At this resolution the carving cannot be read as heraldry — the shape of a shield is legible and nothing inside it is. A proper photograph would settle it.

title: The crenellated tower
caption: «La torre con merlature, ubicata a nord-ovest rispetto alla casa dominicale» — the battlemented tower north-west of the manor, built to watch the property, and badly restored at the end of the twentieth century. It stands at the roadside with a vine over its shoulder.

title: The rustic range behind the house
caption: Arcaded outbuildings in bad repair: the coach house, the produce stores and the colonists' dwellings. The nineteenth-century oil mill stood among these, with its presses and a dozen stone oil jars, until it was converted into a house about twenty years ago.

title: The well
caption: A stone wellhead with an iron arch over it, in what is now a garden. The whole holding was walled, and this stood inside it.

title: The Mione birth index, 1806–1810
caption: «Dipartimento di Passariano, Distretto di Tolmezzo, Cantone di Rigolato, Comune di Mione — Tavola alfabetica per gli Atti di Nascita ch'ebbero luogo dall'anno 1806 all'anno 1810.» The first three lines of the alphabet are Defranceschi Anna-Maria, Defranceschi Anna-Cecilia and De Franceschi Gio: Batta. Four Erman entries follow a few lines down — the other family named in the headmen's list of 1679.
holder: Archivio di Stato di Udine, Stato civile napoleonico, Mione, sig. 12954

title: Anna Maria de Franceschi, Muina, 30 December 1809
caption: Act 32, the last of the year. The midwife Speranza, wife of Antonio Salante, aged fifty-nine, of Muina, presented a girl born that morning at eleven, named Anna Maria — daughter of «Osvaldo de Franceschi e di Appolonia Salante sua consorte, ambedue agricoltori domiciliati in esso villaggio». Registrar: Giacomo Micoli.
holder: Archivio di Stato di Udine, Stato civile napoleonico, Mione, Nati 1809

title: Anna Cecilia de' Franceschi, Mione, 14 January 1810
caption: Act 1 of 1810. «Francesco de' Franceschi d'anni ventisei circa, di professione Sarto» — a tailor, aged about twenty-six — brought his daughter, born that morning at three, and named her Anna Cecilia; her mother is «Margherita nata Gortan sua consorte». He signs the register himself. Act 2 below names Pasqua de' Franceschi, wife of Pietro Luchin of Mione.
holder: Archivio di Stato di Udine, Stato civile napoleonico, Mione, Nati 1810

title: Giovanni Battista De Franceschi, Mione, 15 October 1810
caption: Act 21. «De Franceschi Osualdo d'anni ventisei, di professione fa legname» — a carpenter — presented his son, born at ten that morning in the contrada of Mione, and named him Gio: Batta. The mother is «Cattarina nata Brencis sua consorte». Witnesses: a shoemaker and a tailor, both of Luint. He signs.
holder: Archivio di Stato di Udine, Stato civile napoleonico, Mione, Nati 1810

title: The Mione marriage index, 1806–1810
caption: Two De Franceschi marriages in one small book. The first line of the alphabet: «Salante Appolonia con Defranceschi Osualdo — di Muina — 28 Gennajo 1808». Further down: «Prencis Valentina con Defranceschi Osualdo — di Mione — 6 Agosto 1807».
holder: Archivio di Stato di Udine, Stato civile napoleonico, Mione, sig. 12987

title: Osvaldo de Franceschi marries Appolonia Salante, 28 January 1808
caption: The deepest document in this archive. Osvaldo de Franceschi, farmer, aged twenty, of Muina, «figlio di Antonio de Franceschi, e di Maria nata Corva, pure agricoltori», marries Appolonia Salante, aged twenty-five and a half, daughter of Antonio Salante and Speranza née Micoli. His birth act is read out: born 14 March 1788 at Muina, «da legittimo Matrimonio di Antonio qm. Leonardo de Franceschi, e di Maria nata Corva» — Antonio, son of the late Leonardo. His father's written consent is dated 25 October 1807. Four witnesses, three of them Micoli of Muina. Both spouses sign.
holder: Archivio di Stato di Udine, Stato civile napoleonico, Mione, Matrimoni 1808, atto 1

title: Giacoma de Franceschi marries, 7 August 1806
caption: The earliest De Franceschi act found in Carnia. At Mione, in the «Distretto della Carnia, Cantone di Gorto», Giacoma de Franceschi — seventeen years, two months and twelve days old, «figlia del fu Osualdo de Franceschi, e di Catterina nata Fabris» — marries Ignazio di Prato, a merchant of Chialina. Her birth act of 25 May 1789 is read into the record. She signs herself «Giacoma de Franceschi q.m Osualdo». All four witnesses are tailors; the registrar is Giovanni Micoli-Toscano and the secretary Battà Micoli-Toscano.
holder: Archivio di Stato di Udine, Stato civile napoleonico, Mione, Matrimoni 1806

title: The Mione death index, 1806–1810
caption: Eight Defranceschi entries: Maria 1807, Lucia and Francesco Antonio 1808, Leonarda 1808, Anna Cecilia in January 1810 eleven days after her birth, Sebastiano «chierico» in July 1810, Maddalena in August and Mariana in September. Corva and Erman entries stand among them.
holder: Archivio di Stato di Udine, Stato civile napoleonico, Mione, sig. 12966

title: The Omiš descent chart
caption: A hand-compiled chart of the Omiš and Zadar family, twenty generations deep, running from the fourteenth century to the twentieth. The later generations are omitted from this archive because the people in them may be living.

title: Defranceschi at Bakar, 1783
caption: A register page kept with the family's research notes, placing the name at Bakar on the Kvarner coast in 1783.

title: Moncalvo di Pisino
caption: Gologorica under its Italian name — Moncalvo in the county of Pazin, where Carlo De Franceschi was born in 1809.

title: Seget, near Umag
caption: The western-Istrian estate of the other branch, which reached Istria from Crete after the Candian War ended in 1669.
